title: Airbnb is working on an AI travel agent
title_bn: Airbnb is working on an AI travel agent
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Airbnb plans to roll out an AI agent in the first half of 2027 that will help users plan and book travel, the company said in its Q3 2026 earnings shareholder letter released today. "Today's AI agents are good at simple, routine tasks, like making a
paragraph1: The travel company is planning an “AI-native” trip-planning experience that’s set to roll out next year.The travel company is planning an “AI-native” trip-planning experience that’s set to roll out next year.by Jay PetersNov 6, 2026, 12:06 AM UTCImage: Alex Castro / The VergeJay Peters is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.
paragraph2: Airbnb plans to roll out an AI agent in the first half of 2027 that will help users plan and book travel, the company said in its Q3 2026 earnings shareholder letter released today.“Today’s AI agents are good at simple, routine tasks, like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment,” Airbnb said. “But planning a trip on Airbnb is different.” The company argued that its experience matching hosts and guests, its current role in being part of reservations already, and a “new interface” built “specifically for travel” gives it an edge.
paragraph3: Here’s how Airbnb says that new interface will work:We don’t think a traditional chatbot is the right way to plan a trip. We’re developing a custom-designed, AI-native experience that builds the interface around your question. Rather than a chat window, our agent draws on a library of hundreds of travel-specific interface elements—maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, itineraries—and composes them in real time to match what you’re looking for. Our agent will help guests explore options, make decisions with the people they’re traveling with, and take action directly in Airbnb.
paragraph4: Airbnb co-founder and CEO Brian Chesky has said before that the company plans to launch an agent in 2027, telling the Skift Global Forum that it would have an interface that’s “much richer than a chatbot.”In its shareholder letter, Airbnb also said that AI is “the best thing to ever happen to Airbnb” and has changed how it develops products and operates.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.Jay PetersThe Verge DailyA free daily digest of the news that matters most.

author: TechPulse
excerpt: It's Friday, November 6 in Australia and New Zealand, which means customers who preordered a PROLED touchscreen MacBook Pro, OLED iPad mini, M6 ‌MacBook Pro‌, or M6 iMac are now starting to receive their devices. People will soon be sharing photos an
paragraph1: Thursday November 5, 2026 3:12 pm PST by Juli CloverIt's Friday, November 6 in Australia and New Zealand, which means customers who preordered a PROLED touchscreen MacBook Pro, OLED iPad mini, M6 ‌MacBook Pro‌, or M6 iMac are now starting to receive their devices. People will soon be sharing photos and first impressions of the new products on the MacRumors forums, Reddit, Instagram, and other platforms, giving us a first look at what real-world users think of the ‌OLED‌ upgrade for the ‌iPad mini‌ and the PROLED and touchscreen update for the ‌MacBook Pro‌. Apple's new high-end ‌MacBook Pro‌ models come with M5 Pro or M5 Max, and the major change is the display. It's touch-enabled and is the first Mac with an ‌OLED‌ display. The design has been updated, so the new machines are thinner and lighter than the mini-LED models, which Apple is still selling. Apple also brought back the glowing Apple logo, and replaced the notch with a Dynamic Island.
paragraph2: Pricing on the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model. The ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad mini‌ is Apple's first smaller-screened iPad to get ‌OLED‌, and it's also the most affordable ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad‌. It's almost a millimeter thinner than the prior version and has an Acoustic Display that does away with speaker holes. Without them, the enclosure is sealed, making it the first ‌iPad‌ with a water and dust resistance rating (IP67). It uses Apple's A20 Pro chip. The ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad mini‌ starts at $699.
paragraph3: The 14-inch entry-level ‌MacBook Pro‌ and 24-inch ‌iMac‌ got little in the way of updates beyond an M6 chip. The ‌MacBook Pro‌ is priced starting at $1,999, and the ‌iMac‌ starts at $1,499. Australia is the first country where customers can buy one of the new products in an Apple retail location. Online orders of the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ don't ship until late November or early December, so it's possible in-store stock will be limited. The ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad mini‌, 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌, and ‌iMac‌ should be readily available. After Australia and New Zealand, sales and deliveries of the new Macs and ‌iPad mini‌ will begin in Asia, the Middle East, Europe, and finally, North America.

title: Motorola introduces Polar-powered Moto Watch 2 Fit and Bose-boosted Moto Buds 2 Ultra
title_bn: Motorola introduces Polar-powered Moto Watch 2 Fit and Bose-boosted Moto Buds 2 Ultra
author: TechPulse
excerpt: They pair well with the Motorola Signature 27.
paragraph1: MotorolaAdd Android Authority on Google: TL;DR Motorola expands the ecosystem around the Motorola Signature 27 with the Moto Watch 2 Fit and the Moto Buds 2 Ultra. The Moto Watch 2 Fit has Polar-powered insights, while the Moto Buds 2 Ultra have Bose SoundDesign tuning and Bose QuietControl active noise cancellation. The fitness tracker and earbuds will be available in the coming weeks. Fresh off the launch of the premium Motorola Signature 27 phone, Motorola has introduced two new products that pair with it: the Moto Watch 2 Fit and the Moto Buds 2 Ultra. The Moto Watch 2 Fit adds Polar tracking to the Fit line, while the Moto Buds 2 Ultra have Bose SoundDesign tuning and Bose QuietControl active noise cancellation.The Moto Watch 2 Fit shuns the screenless fitness tracker trend with a 1.
paragraph2: 85-inch OLED screen and Gorilla Glass 3 protection, surrounded by a 2mm bezel. The display is always-on enabled, and has 1,500 nits peak brightness and a 60Hz refresh rate. Motorola said the battery is rated for up to 12 days. As a fitness tracker, the ability to handle dirt, dust, and water is key, and the Moto Watch 2 Fit has IP68 protection and 5ATM water resistance, which Motorola says can sustain splashes, rain, everyday water exposures, and a “brief workout” in a pool.The Moto Watch 2 Fit is outfitted with what you’d expect from a fitness tracker: step and distance counters, heart rate monitoring, vital signs tracking, SpO2 monitoring, stress insights, menstrual cycle tracking, and activity detection that tracks more than 100 workouts.As for the Polar-powered insights, they include a brand-new Running Index to track aerobic efficiency and running progress week over week.
paragraph3: A personalized Daily Activity Score and Daily Activity Goal give insights into activity and targets to reach. There’s also a breakdown of Active Intensity Zones, showing how much time is spent in various heart rate zones, alongside Energy Sources insights that provide metabolic insights about workouts.There are also more wellness-inspired Polar-powered features, including ones for sleep, like a Serene mode for breathing exercises with biofeedback, Nightly Recharge for sleep quality measurement, and Sleep Plus Stages to analyze sleep stages. For waking hours, there’s an Inactivity Alert to encourage movement and a Smart Calories feature to calculate calories burned.While it won’t be available at launch, Motorola said it’s working on an Ask Anything AI-powered feature for workout guidance that will respond to a “Hey Qira” request.Aside from the fitness and wellness features, users can take calls on the Moto Watch 2 Fit.
paragraph4: The Moto Watch 2 Fit is coming to Europe, the Middle East, Latin America, North America, and Asia-Pacific in the coming weeks. In some markets, the Moto Watch 2 Fit will be called the Moto Watch Fit 27. It will be available in three Pantone colors: Stratified Sea, Pigeon, and Ballerina, and the price will start at €119 (~$133).MotorolaThe Moto Buds 2 Ultra have 11mm drivers and Transparency Mode to allow ambient sound in with audio for safety. Dolby Atmos and Dolby Head Tracking make for a more immersive experience. There’s also AI-powered live translation with compatible Motorola phones.
paragraph5: Motorola says that the Moto Buds 2 Ultra get up to eight hours of continuous playback on one charge and up to 37 hours total with the charging case. They have IP57 protection.The Moto Buds 2 Ultra will be available in Europe, the Middle East, Latin America, North America, and Asia-Pacific in the coming weeks. In some markets they’ll be called the Moto Buds Ultra 27. They’ll sell for €199 (~$223).

title: Airbnb says it’s launching an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027
title_bn: Airbnb says it’s launching an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Airbnb says its upcoming AI agent will help travelers plan trips, compare options, manage bookings, and get assistance throughout their stay.
paragraph1: Airbnb has teased its plans to build its own AI travel agent before, but on Thursday the company announced that the new AI feature will launch in the first half of 2027. In the company’s Q3 shareholder letter on Thursday, Airbnb also provided more detail about how the agent will work, what it will actually do, and how it’s different from a typical AI chatbot. In prior interviews, CEO Brian Chesky sketched out the travel company’s approach to AI, describing a plan to build an AI agent that has a richer interface than a conventional chatbot. He also expressed his opinions about how chatbots aren’t the right interface for travel, noting that people take pleasure in the planning process and in anticipating a trip. Any agent that it built, then, shouldn’t take away from the inspiration and the browsing, he told TechCrunch in an interview last month. Chesky today reiterated that belief, telling analysts on the earnings call that people won’t use one AI agent for everything. “Today’s AI agents like Muse and Instinct are good at simple routine tasks like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment. But planning a trip is different,” he said. “Travel is aspirational.
paragraph2: Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience. In fact, 80% of travelers say they enjoy spending time researching trips. People want to look at photos. They want to compare homes. They want to make decisions with people they’re traveling with,” he continued. “And I don’t think the general-purpose agents are the best to do that. So that is why we are building our own AI agent,” Chesky said. Airbnb described its agent as having a personalized interface that’s designed specifically for travel, where it will “build an interface” around a user’s question instead of simply responding as a chatbot would. “What we are doing is developing a custom-designed AI-native experience that responds to what guests are looking for,” Chesky said.
paragraph3: “So instead of relying on traditional chat alone, which is very text-heavy — which, again, is definitely not the way you should plan travel, our agent draws from a library of hundreds of travel-specific interface components — maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, itineraries — and composes them in real time to match what they’re looking for.” The exec said the agent will feel “a little bit like generative UI” as it’s designed to offer up “the right interface at the right time” for someone’s specific travel needs. In its shareholder letter, the company touted that its nearly 20 years of experience in bringing hosts and guests together is informing how the agent is built, as it incorporates insights about how people both book and host on its platform. The agent will also be able to help travelers beyond the booking itself. “Our agent will be able to help guests throughout their trip — from changing a reservation or resolving a payment issue to getting help with refunds, rebooking, or 24-hour safety support. Services and experiences are two areas that have become a bigger focus for the company following its redesign last year. title: Samsung One UI 9.5 brings notable changes to Health and Calendar
title_bn: Samsung One UI 9.5 brings notable changes to Health and Calendar
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Calendar could lose its grid, Health could gain a journal.
paragraph1: Aamir Siddiqui / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: TL;DR Early One UI 9.5 test builds reveal upcoming changes to Samsung Calendar and Samsung Health. Samsung Calendar is getting a cleaner, grid-free interface, a relocated search button, and a new Key events section. Samsung Health is gaining Mindful note, a new journaling feature with guided prompts and daily reminders. Samsung’s One UI 9 rollout is still underway, but that isn’t stopping the South Korean tech giant from preparing its next big software update. With One UI 9.
paragraph2: 5 currently in development, and an early beta build for the Galaxy S26 Ultra already spotted on a test server, we’re starting to inch closer to Samsung’s second Android 17-based update.Samsung hasn’t detailed what’s coming with the update, but that hasn’t stopped testers from getting their hands on the unreleased software and uncovering the changes.The latest discoveries shed light on two first-party apps: Samsung Health and Samsung Calendar, both of which appear to be getting some love with One UI 9.5, as highlighted by SamMobile.Samsung Calendar The image on the left highlights what Google Calendar looks like with One UI 9, while the image on the right highlights what it could look like with One UI 9.5.
paragraph3: There are three main notable changes here. For starters, Samsung appears to have removed the individual rectangular backgrounds surrounding each date, so instead of appearing against a contrasting cell, dates now simply float against a black background. This makes the boundaries between dates much less obvious. At the same time, it gives the view a lot more room to breathe.Secondly, the search button has been relocated from the top right of the view to the bottom right, sitting right next to the Add event pill. Speaking of which, the pill itself now surfaces less text.
paragraph4: It only says “Add event” without referencing the currently selected date.Elsewhere, the search screen now also appears to highlight a new Key events section, which reportedly displays important events as pill-shaped shortcuts. As seen in the second screenshot above, the section will appear above the existing calendar and color menus. And as seen in the last image above, the app’s sidebar is being reorganized too. The Sync now, Recycle bin, and Settings options now appear to have been relocated above the account list.Samsung HealthSamMobileThe updated Samsung Health offers some UI changes, but the bigger addition here is Mindful note, a new in-app journaling feature.
paragraph5: The addition aims to offer Samsung users a safe place to reflect, note down thoughts, and “capture a moment, a feeling, or whatever comes to mind.”You have the option to start with a blank slate or get some ideas with prompts, including About yourself, Relationships, Work and goals, and What if…? There’s also an option to set reminders, which should come in handy if you’re trying to make journaling a daily habit.The changes mentioned above have only been spotted in prerelease software. These might never make it out widely, and if they do, they might or might not look and function as described here.

title: Serve Robotics launches new business to become the AWS for robots
title_bn: Serve Robotics launches new business to become the AWS for robots
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Serve Robotics announced alonsgside its third-quarter earnings that it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services to offer customers its connectivity and data tools.
paragraph1: Serve Robotics, a maker of self-driving sidewalk delivery robots, is expanding beyond its autonomous delivery operations in a bid to become a technology supplier to other companies building robots. The company, which spun out of Uber’s acquisition of Postmates in 2021 and went public in 2024, said Thursday it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services. Specifically, Serve Robotics will offer customers its connectivity and data tools. Bedrock Robotics, a startup developing self-driving systems for construction equipment, is a customer, according to Serve. It’s also working with T-Mobile to bring AI computing power closer to robots, Serve announced alongside its third-quarter earnings on Thursday. “We are solving the problem of robots in human spaces,” Serve Robotics CEO and co-founder Ali Kashani told TechCrunch.
paragraph2: Serve Robotics already makes two kinds of robots, the cute googly-eyed sidewalk delivery robot and one designed for hospitals that it got through its acquisition of Diligent Robotics. Those businesses are not going away, Kashani emphasized in a recent interview. Instead, he said there is opportunity to sell the technology it developed for its own robots to other companies developing robots for farms, warehouses, and other uncontrolled environments. “I kind of think of it as the AWS moment where we are taking the technology we’ve built for us, and we’re opening it up for more people to build on,” he said, adding this wouldn’t have been possible without developing its own robot fleet. The expansion comes as Serve’s sidewalk delivery business expands, but is shifting away from Uber and toward other partners, including DoorDash and Wonder. Its new Physical AI Services business line will offer three products.
paragraph3: Serve Link helps connect robots in the field to AI systems running in data centers, which would allow companies to potentially tap into more powerful AI models without having to put all that computing power onboard. “Any robotic application generally needs to connect the robots to some offline intelligence, whether it’s to collect data or do exception handling or whatever,” said Kashani. “It’s the connectivity piece that has to be really high performance. You need to be able to manage really unreliable networks and still reliably connect, and that’s what we solve.” It’s also launching a data curator tool that helps companies find edge cases in the reams of real-world data a robot collects, which can then be fed back into a training model to improve performance. Its third product is a real-world, foundation-model data catalog built from Serve’s own sidewalk robots that can teach AI models how to understand complex human environments.
paragraph4: Kashani said he’s been thinking about this idea — a playbook he learned from Amazon — for years. “When the technology is so nascent, you have got to build the end-to-end application because that’s the only way you know what to build, but then over time, as the technology gets more advanced, a lot more people are going to be wanting to build similar things,” he said. “And what you want to do is to open your technology so others build with you and on your platform.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. title: CEO Harsh Jain Teases A Revamped Dream11 By 2026-End
title_bn: CEO Harsh Jain Teases A Revamped Dream11 By 2026-End
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Erstwhile real money gaming (RMG) giant Dream11’s cofounder and CEO Harsh Jain has hinted at plans to launch a revamped…
paragraph1: SUMMARYJain said that the “brand new Dream11” would be built by sports fans and for sports fans. He did not disclose the upcoming platform’s features, commercial model or a specific launch date The move signals Dream11’s next phase of evolution after the ban on online real-money gaming last year disrupted the platform’s paid fantasy sports business This comes as Dream11 has been rethinking many of its newer bets. In the past year, the startup has shut down Dream Money, Dream Play and FanCode’s sports merchandise business Erstwhile real money gaming (RMG) giant Dream11’s cofounder and CEO Harsh Jain has hinted at plans to launch a revamped version of the platform by 2026-end. In a post on social media platform X, Jain said that the “brand new Dream11” would be built by sports fans and for sports fans. He did not disclose the upcoming platform’s features, commercial model or a specific launch date.
paragraph2: “A brand new Dream11 is launching (at the) end of Dec – by sports fans, for sports fans. Stay tuned…,” said Jain in his post. The move signals Dream11’s next phase of evolution after the ban on online real-money gaming last year disrupted the platform’s paid fantasy sports business. While the teaser points to a product overhaul, it remains unclear how substantially the new offering will differ from its existing services. This comes more than a year after the Parliament passed the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025, which prohibited online real money games and restricted their promotion and advertising.
paragraph3: Following the legislation, Dream11 discontinued paid contests and pivoted to a watch-along platform where users can follow gameplays of prominent content creators. It has also been exploring alternative ways to engage sports fans. Last year, parent Dream Sports forayed into the wealth tech space under Dream Money and began offering mutual funds, digital gold, fixed deposits, and loans. It later also forayed into stockbroking with DreamStreet and forayed into the SaaS space with Dream Horizon. However, it has been rethinking many of its newer bets.
paragraph4: The startup shut down Dream Money in June this year. Dream Sports also quietly shut FanCode’s sports merchandise business earlier this year amid persistent issues with commercial viability. It also shut down its AI-powered sports performance analytics app Dream Play in June this year. Nevertheless, the startup’s portfolio still remains substantial. FanCode continues to operate as a sports streaming platform, while DreamCricket represents its push into AAA gaming.
paragraph5: It also has its investment platform DreamStreet. Beyond the business challenges, Dream Sports is also facing GST dues of more than ₹20,000 Cr. In a blow to the company, the Supreme Court (SC), earlier this year, also upheld the tax authorities’ move to impose a 28% retrospective GST on real money online gaming companies over the full face value of bets placed through their platforms.

title: Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar
title_bn: Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Meta's AI agent can now take calls as a customizable animated avatar, ahead of the launch of a Tamagotchi-like wearable designed to bring Muse to life.
paragraph1: Muse Voice, a feature that lets users call and video chat with Meta’s consumer AI agent, Muse, is now available to everyone in the U.S., the company announced on Thursday. First introduced at Meta’s Connect developer conference in September, the video-chatting feature involves new AI models, Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice technology, which help power the digital avatar that chats with the user. While other AI competitors offer voice chat features, Meta’s Muse offers a cute, animated avatar (nicknamed Jolly), which users interact with as they ask questions or request tasks to be handled on their behalf.
paragraph2: Users can also customize the avatar as they choose, changing it to something that looks more like a person, animal, or some other character. The company believes that anthropomorphizing Muse in this way could make consumers feel more connected to their AI agent — a connection that could grow even stronger as they begin to engage in live conversations with it. As the Muse avatar speaks, Meta says it will use “subtle expressions and gestures” that match the tone of the conversation. (Muse doesn’t actually “see” the user, but it hears them and reacts based on their conversations.) The news of the rollout was announced via blog post and on X by Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, who shared a demo of his Muse in action.
paragraph3: The video saw Wang joking around, referencing his love of posting memes on X, which he told his Muse may have gotten him in trouble with his boss. His Muse, a fluffy white dog, responds with a suggestion to add disclaimers to those memes that could be misinterpreted as Meta endorsing anything risqué. (Ha!) The added support for video chats and calls comes just before Meta’s plan to launch a Tamagotchi-like wearable device for its Muse AI agent before year-end. When the device arrives, the digital avatar will appear on its small screen, letting users talk to the agent, which can then reply or carry out tasks for them.
paragraph4: Meta says the real-time conversations are supported on mobile, web, and Mac and will later come to its AI Glasses and the upcoming “Muse Charm” hardware device. title: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
title_bn: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
author: TechPulse
excerpt: OpenAI's newest cybersecurity model comes out as AI labs face scrutiny of their work to protect digital infrastructure.
paragraph1: Max Justicz, the chief technology officer and co-founder of the startup Charge Robotics, used an OpenAI model to find a severe vulnerability that — if exploited — could allow hackers to take control of servers running Ubuntu, a widely used open source Linux-based operating system. Justicz, who has a hobbyist’s interest in cybersecurity and previously found a vulnerability in the same codebase, told TechCrunch that he found this issue using GPT 5.6 Sol, released in July, through the AI maker’s Daybreak Blue, a program that gives cybersecurity defenders access to powerful frontier models. “I literally just aimed ChatGPT at the same body of code and said ‘I found this bug previously that was fixed several years ago, please find bugs as bad or worse,’ and it came back in two hours with this,” Justicz said. “It’s extremely convoluted and hard for a human to find, but it works!” He reported the issue to the Debian Project, which maintains the software in question and issued a patch to fix the vulnerability. There has been no known evidence of exploitation. Still, the ease with which he found it suggests that we’ve only seen the tip of the iceberg when it comes to potential exploits that even novice hackers can utilize with the help of AI models.
paragraph2: “I can only imagine what one could do with more time and access to less neutered models. We should expect some extremely crazy bugs to be found and exploited over the next few months,” Justicz wrote in a social media thread discussing his finding. “This might be obvious to most folks here, but there is currently huge alpha in taking some code or binary someone has not audited yet and just aiming a powerful AI model at it.” OpenAI appears to have noticed. Today, the AI giant announced a new model focused on cybersecurity, ChatGPT Cyber, would be made available to the highest tier of users in the cybersecurity program, Daybreak Red, which allows offensive cybersecurity researchers tools for vulnerability hunting and development. Yesterday, OpenAI said that the same model had been used to scan and prepare patches for vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel, finding 948 potential issues. OpenAI also found 81 “novel” vulnerabilities in Firefox, the web browser. “Our goal is to dramatically expand Daybreak, bringing advanced security research to organizations of every size, independent researchers, and open-source maintainers,” the frontier lab said in a statement.
paragraph3: OpenAI has insisted that there is a narrow window of time for the people who safeguard digital infrastructure to take action before AI models become even better at hacking and easier to access. For cyber defenders, however, it can feel like the frontier labs have unleashed a mountain of new work that outstrips their resources. Justicz said that he personally spent about $5,000 on subscriptions and tokens to find several exploits. Besides Daybreak’s model access, OpenAI has also announced a $1 billion initiative to support cybersecurity professionals in the program who work on critical infrastructure like the electrical grid or water systems. The Daybreak program has its own critiques. Justicz notes that the frontier lab appears to have recently “nerfed” Daybreak Blue to make it less useful at finding vulnerabilities. On one hand, it may be good to limit access from potential bad actors — Justicz said he just uploaded a photo of his driver’s license to join the program. On the other, cybersecurity professionals say they have one hand tied if they can’t use frontier technology while bad actors can deploy open-weight models with abliterated guardrails.
paragraph4: Still, OpenAI says just “thousands” of cybersecurity professionals are participating in the Daybreak program, versus a far larger number of potential hackers. It’s unclear if frontier labs are devoting enough of their resources to this issue. Eric Wallace, a researcher on OpenAI’s technical staff, said that “we are now allocating a significant amount of our frontier compute towards discovering and patching vulnerabilities in open source codebases, fully pro bono.” But the Linux bug hunt cost $1.2 million, which is significantly less than the approximate $6 million token spend the company invested in finding a potential solution to a famous problem of fluid dynamics. If there is a narrow window of time to patch the digital infrastructure the world depends on, more urgency may be required. title: Paid $200 for Logic Pro? Apple Says You Won't Get This New Feature
title_bn: Paid $200 for Logic Pro? Apple Says You Won't Get This New Feature
author: TechPulse
excerpt: According to Apple's full release notes for version 13.0 of Logic Pro for Mac, released today, the new AI-powered Intelligent Assistant feature requires an Apple Creator Studio subscription for $12.99 per month or $129 per year. In other words, the f
paragraph1: Thursday November 5, 2026 9:51 am PST by Joe RossignolAccording to Apple's full release notes for version 13.0 of Logic Pro for Mac, released today, the new AI-powered Intelligent Assistant feature requires an Apple Creator Studio subscription for $12.99 per month or $129 per year. In other words, the feature is not available in the $199.99 one-time purchase version of Logic Pro. Apple's fine print on the Logic Pro release notes page: The intelligent assistant (beta) requires an Apple Creator Studio subscription, a Mac with Apple silicon, and macOS 27 or later.
paragraph2: Indeed, the release notes for the one-time purchase version of Logic Pro for Mac version 13.0 do not mention Intelligent Assistant. The subscription requirement was not mentioned in Apple's announcement last month: The assistant (beta) in Logic Pro for Mac requires macOS 27 Golden Gate or later on an Apple Intelligence-capable Mac and is available in U.S. English only. Apple customers who are growing tired of features being locked behind a subscription will obviously be disappointed to learn this news.
paragraph3: Logic Pro's Intelligent Assistant likely requires a Creator Studio subscription because it uses cloud AI models. In a support document, Apple said the feature will have monthly usage limits, with expanded usage available for a fee. Apple says the Intelligent Assistant is powered by a combination of Apple-built and third-party AI models. The feature is designed to help creators "navigate production workflows, start a new song, set up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refine an active project." Except for creators who opted to pay $199.99 upfront for Logic Pro, that is.

title: Garmin isn’t ready to abandon power-efficient MIP displays on wearables, even as AMOLED improves
title_bn: Garmin isn’t ready to abandon power-efficient MIP displays on wearables, even as AMOLED improves
author: TechPulse
excerpt: AMOLED is catching up, but one important advantage is keeping MIP alive.
paragraph1: Ryan Haines / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: TL;DR Garmin COO Brad Trenkle says MIP displays aren’t disappearing anytime soon because they still offer advantages in battery life and outdoor visibility. Although Garmin’s AMOLED watches are becoming more power-efficient, they haven’t completely closed the endurance gap with MIP models. Garmin also sees potential for solar-powered OLED watches, although no such product has been announced. A quiet tug-of-war is happening on Garmin wrists. On one side, AMOLED displays are winning hearts with their rich colors, crisp graphics, and gorgeous watch faces.
paragraph2: On the other, the less glamorous memory-in-pixel (MIP) screens are still winning endurance contests, especially when the sun is blazing and the nearest charger is miles away. Garmin is increasingly embracing the former, but it isn’t ready to retire the latter.Speaking to TechRadar, Garmin COO Brad Trenkle explained that battery life remains the biggest reason MIP displays still have a place in the company’s smartwatch lineup.Unlike AMOLED screens, which produce their own light, MIP displays take advantage of ambient light to remain visible. That makes them particularly useful outdoors, where bright sunlight helps readability rather than forcing the screen to work harder.
paragraph3: And Garmin has some compelling evidence sitting in its own product catalog.The recently launched Enduro 4 sticks with a MIP display and boasts up to 90 days of battery life in smartwatch mode with sufficient solar charging. Meanwhile, the Instinct 3 offers a choice between a colorful AMOLED screen and a solar-powered MIP alternative that can theoretically keep running indefinitely under ideal conditions.That doesn’t mean AMOLED is standing still. Garmin’s Fenix 9 Pro already boasts a stunning display that can reach 3,000 nits, and Trenkle acknowledges that OLED battery efficiency keeps improving with each generation.
paragraph4: However, he says the battery-life gap between the two technologies “has not completely converged,” which is why Garmin doesn’t expect MIP to disappear entirely just yet.Garmin isn’t ruling out combining OLED displays with solar charging either. Trenkle explained that some of the company’s solar technology collects energy through a ring surrounding the display rather than placing a layer over the screen itself. That approach could let an OLED watch harvest sunlight without compromising display quality. However, Garmin hasn’t announced such a product, and there’s no indication of when one might arrive.
paragraph5: For now, Garmin’s display strategy leaves room for both the watch that looks spectacular at a glance and the one that refuses to quit halfway through an adventure. OLED keeps getting better, but MIP still has one particularly persuasive argument: fewer encounters with a charging cable.

title: Samsung Galaxy Fit 4 app listing hints at NFC payment support
title_bn: Samsung Galaxy Fit 4 app listing hints at NFC payment support
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Despite the tracker's FCC filing omitting NFC.
paragraph1: Kaitlyn Cimino / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: TL;DR Samsung’s Galaxy Fit 4 Manager app has appeared on the Galaxy Store, revealing a dedicated Wallet option that hints at contactless payment support. However, the tracker’s earlier FCC certification makes no mention of NFC connectivity, leaving payment support uncertain. The listing also showcases new watch faces and a battery life estimate of just over four days, though the latter is likely placeholder data. Samsung’s fitness wearable ambitions don’t appear to be slowing down any time soon. Last month, we shared video clips of the upcoming Galaxy Fit 4 from 360-degree angles, and although the wearable looked almost indistinguishable from its predecessor on the outside, new leaks suggest that it could have a lot going for it on the inside.
paragraph2: Beyond a trove of new watch faces and stress-tracking support, the upcoming fitness tracker could finally bring contactless payments to the Galaxy Fit line. This should bring Samsung’s offering more in line with competitors like Google’s Fitbit Charge line and Xiaomi’s smart bands, both of which boast NFC for contactless payments.Information about the development comes from Samsung itself. The tech giant published the Galaxy Fit 4 Manager app on the Galaxy Store, and although that doesn’t offer much at first glance, a closer look at the screenshots in the listing reveals a key detail, as pointed out by SamMobile.Galaxy StoreThe screenshot above highlights the Galaxy Fit 4 Manager app’s settings page, and among familiar menus, there’s a new Wallet option hiding in plain sight.

title: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says company could be IPO ready in 2027
title_bn: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says company could be IPO ready in 2027
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Speaking at a Wall Street Journal tech conference on Wednesday, the executive touted how the company had been gaining ground in the enterprise market, where rival Anthropic had already successfully made inroads.
paragraph1: OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman said the company would be ready for an IPO in 2027, noting that its enterprise revenue has been growing. Speaking at a Wall Street Journal tech conference on Wednesday, the executive touted how the company had been gaining ground in the enterprise market, where rival Anthropic had already successfully made inroads. In response to the interviewer’s question about being IPO-ready next year, Brockman replied, “I think so. Yes.” “We’ve been very clear this year that we want to go public when we feel is the right time for us, and I feel extremely good about the business. I feel like we’ve made so much progress this year, and I’ve honestly never felt more confident in what we’re doing,” Brockman said.
paragraph2: He detailed how OpenAI’s trajectory as an enterprise had changed over the course of 2026, noting that the first and second quarters were “pretty rough.” He also admitted that OpenAI “wasn’t even in the conversation” when it came to agentic coding — an area where Anthropic’s Claude Code has gained market share. “We had Codex, but no one was talking about it,” Brockman continued, “and I think that we just kept our heads down and executed.” By the third quarter, activity picked up, as OpenAI saw 70% quarterly growth in its annualized revenue — something Brockman attributed to the enterprise side of the business doubling. He explained that the growth wasn’t simply the result of something that happened in the quarter itself, but rather the culmination of investments the company had been making up to that point. Now the majority of OpenAI’s revenue is coming from the enterprise business, which previously accounted for only around 30% of its total revenue.
paragraph3: “And it’s not that consumer [revenue has shrunk] … It’s been growing, but it’s the enterprise segment has really taken off,” he said, pointing to a recent partnership with JPMorgan Chase as one example of the type of client it’s now winning deals with. Brockman also spoke more broadly about the lessons OpenAI learned from selling into the enterprise market as well. He said the company had come to understand that its job was to help businesses identify the most important milestones they could achieve with its AI technology, build trust with clients, and demonstrate that it was a reliable partner for the long haul. “A year ago, we weren’t even really in the enterprise game, right? We were really perceived as a consumer company, and a lot of the companies we’d start talking to would say, ‘Is OpenAI really committed to the enterprise?’” Brockman said.

title: India targets creating homegrown GPUs within 2 years and plans to commercialize indigenous SHAKTI and VEGA processors
title_bn: India targets creating homegrown GPUs within 2 years and plans to commercialize indigenous SHAKTI and VEGA processors
author: TechPulse
excerpt: MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan says India plans to develop its own GPU under Semiconductor Mission 2.0, with a target of approximately two years. The country is also looking to commercialize its SHAKTI and VEGA RISC-V processors, expand domestic server
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty Images) India wants to develop its own graphics processing unit (GPU) within the next two years as the country steps up efforts to build a domestic semiconductor industry and reduce its dependence on foreign chip suppliers, reports ETGovernment. The target was outlined by S.Krishnan, secretary of India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), in a November 4 interview. "Under India Semiconductor Mission 2.
paragraph2: 0, we intend to target the development of an indigenous GPU chip. We should have a GPU chip of our own. This will not happen overnight. It is a project that will require approximately 24 months, and we intend to work towards that objective," Krishnan said.
paragraph3: The proposed GPU is part of a wider plan to establish an Indian hardware and software ecosystem, with Krishnan describing five layers needed to support AI development. These include: energy, accelerator chips, computing infrastructure and servers, AI models and applications. Indian companies such as VVDN, Kaynes and Avalon are already manufacturing servers, while the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) has developed its Rudra server range, whose systems are designed to support AI workloads, after which the government transfers the technology to local manufacturers. Krishnan also sees AI as a potential repeat of the opportunity India's IT industry experienced during the Y2K (the year 2000 bug) transition.

title: Google Home bug is repeatedly asking some users to set up the app again
title_bn: Google Home bug is repeatedly asking some users to set up the app again
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Some smart homes keep forgetting who's in charge.
paragraph1: Joe Maring / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: TL;DR Some Google Home users say the app repeatedly asks them to sign in or complete setup whenever they open it. Reports dating back to mid-October mention versions 4.34.22 and 4.35.25.1, although the issue doesn’t appear widespread.
paragraph2: No confirmed fix exists, but affected users can try updating to version 4.36.24 or newer. The Google Home app is supposed to remember your smart home devices, but some users say it’s having trouble remembering them. For at least two weeks, the app has been repeatedly welcoming existing users as though they’ve never opened it before, turning a routine trip to their smart home controls into an unexpected account setup exercise.The complaints have been trickling into Reddit discussions and Google’s support forums since mid-October. Instead of landing on their familiar dashboard, affected users say they see a welcome screen whenever they launch Google Home, forcing them to select or set up their Google account before accessing connected devices.
paragraph3: The app isn’t always in a hurry to cooperate, with some users reporting waiting up to 10 minutes for their devices to appear when they skip setup. It’s one of those bugs that easily disrupt your usual habit of controlling smart home devices directly from the lock screen, so we understand the frustration among those affected.The fact that the complaints span multiple Google Home app versions, including v4.34.22 and the newer v4.35.25.
paragraph4: 1, is even more frustrating. However, the issue doesn’t appear widespread. We’ve used the Google Home app regularly on the affected v4.34.22 and even the latest v4.36.24 without encountering the issue.
paragraph5: So if you’re affected, it’s worth checking the Play Store for the latest version. It hasn’t been confirmed as a fix, but it’s a reasonable first step while the cause remains unclear.One user claims Google support acknowledged a known issue following an app update. However, Google has not publicly confirmed this, and community representatives continue directing complaints to support.We’ve reached out to Google for clarification on what’s causing the repeated sign-in prompts, whether the latest app update addresses the problem, and if a broader fix is underway. We’ll update this article if we hear back.

title: YouTube bug makes the app appear in half dark mode, half light
title_bn: YouTube bug makes the app appear in half dark mode, half light
author: TechPulse
excerpt: A bug is causing issues with dark and light mode on YouTube.
paragraph1: Joe Maring / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: TL;DR YouTube viewers are reporting an issue with using the app in light mode and dark mode. The issue causes the playback area and comments section to be displayed in dark mode, while the rest of the screen is in light mode. Both Android and iOS users are experiencing the bug. Some YouTube viewers are reporting a display issue with the mobile app.
paragraph2: The top half of the screen, where the player and comments section are located, is displayed in dark mode. Meanwhile, the rest of the UI is displayed in light mode.According to the reports (1, 2, 3, 4), the bug happens regardless of whether you have dark mode or light mode enabled. Switching Ambient mode on or off reportedly doesn’t have an effect either.
paragraph3: Users have tried restarting the app, restarting their phones, clearing cache, uninstalling and reinstalling the app, and adjusting accessibility settings. Despite taking these measures, the effected users claim that the issue persists.A majority of the reports come from Android users, but the problem is not exclusive to one platform. We also spotted at least one report from an iPhone user.
paragraph4: While there are plenty of new reports, it appears that some viewers have been experiencing this issue for a while.It’s understandable why such a bug would be irritating. If you want apps to be in dark mode, then you want the entire app to be dark and vice versa. A screen split into half dark mode and half light mode kind of defeats the purpose.
paragraph5: Android Authority has reached out to Google for comment. We will update this article when new information becomes available. If you’re experiencing this glitch, let us know in the comments section.

author: TechPulse
excerpt: Insurtech Go Digit reported a 31.1% year-on-year (YoY) decline in its net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) to…
paragraph1: SUMMARYGo Digit General Insurance reported a 31.1% YoY decline in net profit to ₹142.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, while insurance revenue grew 1.7% to ₹2,720.5 Cr. The insurer's insurance service result fell 73.4% YoY to ₹43 Cr as insurance service expenses increased 22.4% to ₹2,607.7 Cr Motor Third Party insurance remained Go Digit’s largest segment, generating ₹1,066.1 Cr in Q2 FY27 revenue, up 8.3% YoY Insurtech Go Digit reported a 31.1% year-on-year (YoY) decline in its net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) to ₹142.4 Cr from ₹206.8 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. The insurtech major’s profit also declined 62.4% sequentially from ₹378.61 Cr in the June quarter. The decline in profitability came despite a marginal increase in insurance revenue, which rose 1.
paragraph2: 7% to ₹2,720.5 Cr during the quarter from ₹2,674.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, insurance revenue increased 2.1% from ₹2,665.6 Cr. Segment-wise, Motor Third Party (TP) insurance remained Go Digit’s largest business, contributing ₹1,066.1 Cr to insurance revenue in Q2 FY27, up 8.3% YoY. Motor Own Damage (OD) insurance revenue grew at a faster pace of 11.4% YoY to ₹640.64 Cr. The company’s gross written premium for the quarter dipped by 3.6% YoY to ₹2,571 Cr while gross direct premium, dipped 1.2% to ₹2,351 Cr. However, the company’s insurance service result, which reflects the profitability of its insurance operations before investment and other financial income, sunk 73.4% YoY to ₹43 Cr from ₹161.98 Cr in the year-ago quarter.
paragraph3: The figure also fell 62.3% sequentially from ₹114 Cr. The deterioration in the insurance service result came as insurance service expenses increased 22.4% YoY to ₹2,607.73 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹2,130.85 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. title: Venomics AI Raises $2.7 Mn To Turn Venom Into Medicine
title_bn: Venomics AI Raises $2.7 Mn To Turn Venom Into Medicine
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Bengaluru-based biotechnology startup Venomics AI has raised $2.7 Mn (around ₹25.5 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Speciale…
paragraph1: SUMMARYBiotechnology startup Venomics AI has raised $2.7 Mn (around ₹25.5 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons The fresh capital will be used to expand ‘Venom Atlas’, a molecular dataset of venom-derived compounds, and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities The startup combines venom biology, AI and experimental screening to identify and develop venom-derived molecules into potential therapeutic leads Bengaluru-based biotechnology startup Venomics AI has raised $2.7 Mn (around ₹25.
paragraph2: 5 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons, with participation from Operators Studio. The startup, spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), combines venom biology, AI and experimental screening to identify and develop venom-derived molecules into potential therapeutic leads. The fresh capital will be used to expand ‘Venom Atlas’, a molecular dataset of venom-derived compounds, and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities. The startup also plans to expand its team across venom biology, computational science and drug discovery, while supporting the validation and optimisation of promising molecules.
paragraph3: Founded in 2026 by Kartik Sunagar and Vinay Prabhu, Venomics AI is working to tap the largely unexplored molecular diversity found in animal venoms to identify potential drug candidates. Animal venoms contain complex molecules that have evolved over millions of years to interact with specific biological targets. Some of these compounds have already inspired medicines. However, a large part of the molecular diversity across venomous species remains unexplored, presenting an opportunity for drug discovery.
paragraph4: Venomics AI is building a platform that combines molecular sequencing and venom biology to map this diversity through its Venom Atlas. It then uses AI to prioritise promising molecular candidates and validates its predictions through functional laboratory screening. “Animal venoms represent one of nature’s richest yet least explored sources of potential medicines, and at Venomics AI, we are combining cutting-edge experimental science with artificial intelligence to unlock this extraordinary potential,” Sunagar said. India’s bioeconomy is on track to reach $300 Bn by 2030, with the country’s rapid emergence as a global biotechnology hub, based on IBEF data.
paragraph5: Notably, the biotech sector in the country has been booming in recent years. The country is home to more than 11,000 biotech startups. Also, as part of the Budget 2027, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced a new ‘Biopharma SHAKTI’ scheme with an outlay of ₹10,000 Cr. Meanwhile, investor interest in this space has been gradually seeing an uptick, where earlier this year, Cellogen Therapeutics secured ₹20 Cr in funding from Kotak Alternate Asset Managers (Kotak Alts), while StrainX Bioworks has raised $13 Mn in a funding round led by Prime Venture Partners and Leo Capital.

title: Micron's $4.5 billion Taoyuan plant construction halted amidst labor dispute
title_bn: Micron's $4.5 billion Taoyuan plant construction halted amidst labor dispute
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Micron and the Taoyuan labor union is set to meet again on November 6 as the two parties engage in a protracted labor dispute regarding profit-sharing.
paragraph1: Micron has paused construction on its Fab 11E site at Taoyuan as the company and its Taoyuan labor union have failed to reach an agreement regarding clearer profit-sharing terms. Bloomberg reports that activity on the site has all but halted, except for minor safety work, with some sources saying that executives are concerned about uncertainties regarding negotiations with its workers.
paragraph2: The company hasn’t released a statement about the move but has already informed local officials about the suspension.“Taiwan plays an important role in Micron’s global footprint, and our operations today continue as normal,” Micron said.
paragraph3: “We are confident in maintaining business continuity for our customers.” The company has recently announced a bonus that could give as much as five times the annual salary of some eligible workers, and has also wrapped up a deal with the bigger Taichung union, although some members say they were dissatisfied with the outcome.
paragraph4: On the other hand, the Taoyuan union is still holding out for better terms, with the two parties set to meet again on November 6. It even launched a one-day strike last month to show the chipmaker its resolve and how its operations could be disrupted if it does not meet their demands.

title: SaaS Company RateGain’s Q2 Profit Rises 47% YoY To ₹75 Cr
title_bn: SaaS Company RateGain’s Q2 Profit Rises 47% YoY To ₹75 Cr
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Travel-focused SaaS company RateGain reported a 46.5% increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹74.7 Cr in the September quarter…
paragraph1: SUMMARYRateGain reported a consolidated net profit of ₹74.7 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 46.5% YoY, while operating revenue jumped 152.6% to ₹745.4 Cr. The consolidation of Sojern significantly expanded RateGain’s revenue and expenses, with marketing technology now accounting for 80.2% of its revenue. RateGain’s UK subsidiary repaid another $46.3 Mn today, reducing the outstanding acquisition-related debt to $31.3 Mn, a quarter of the original facility. Travel-focused SaaS company Rategain reported a 46.5% increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹74.7 Cr in the September quarter (Q2 FY27) from ₹51 Cr a year ago. Operating revenue jumped 152.6% YoY to ₹745.4 Cr, reflecting the consolidation of travel marketing platform Sojern, which RateGain acquired for $250 Mn in November last year.
paragraph2: Sequentially, net profit declined 21.3% from ₹94.9 Cr, while operating revenue fell 5% from ₹785 Cr. RateGain reported negative other income of ₹26.2 Lakh, taking its total income to ₹745.1 Cr. Total expenses rose about 158% YoY to ₹647.7 Cr. Adjusted for deferred deal consideration related to the Sojern acquisition, RateGain said its net profit rose 78% YoY to ₹90.8 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to ₹169.1 Cr. For H1 FY27, operating revenue increased 169.5% YoY to ₹1,530.4 Cr from ₹568 Cr. Reported EBITDA rose 214.2% to ₹324.
paragraph3: 5 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA increased 250.9% to ₹362.5 Cr. The company said its reported H1 EBITDA had already exceeded its full-year FY26 EBITDA. Sojern Integration And Debt The Sojern acquisition expanded RateGain’s travel marketing business, particularly its presence among destination marketing organisations (DMOs), hotels, and other travel businesses. To finance the acquisition, RateGain’s UK subsidiary secured a $125 Mn debt facility from HSBC and Citibank, backed by a corporate guarantee from the Indian parent. Including a repayment of $46.3 Mn today, the subsidiary has repaid $93.8 Mn, or 75%, of the original facility. Its outstanding debt now stands at $31.3 Mn. Alongside the expansion in revenue, RateGain said the Sojern integration helped broaden its customer base. It had 14,538 customers at the end of September, about 4.5X the 3,224 customers it had at the end of FY25. Its customers include hospitality companies, online travel agencies (OTAs), airlines, car rental companies, and DMOs. Marketing Drives Business Mix RateGain operates across three verticals: data as a service (DaaS), distribution, and marketing technology.
paragraph4: Its offerings span competitive pricing and demand intelligence, hotel distribution, digital marketing, and guest engagement. Marketing technology now accounts for 80.2% of revenue, followed by DaaS at 13.2% and distribution at 6.6%. By customer industry, hospitality contributed 48.6% of H1 revenue, followed by DMOs at 30.9%, OTAs at 7.2%, airlines at 3.7%, and car rentals at 2.3%. North America accounted for 63.7% of H1 revenue, followed by Europe at 21.5%, Asia-Pacific at 12.3%, and other markets at 2.5%.
paragraph5: The company’s client roster includes 33 of the world’s top 40 hotel chains, four of the top five airlines, and seven of the top 10 car rental companies. RateGain also highlighted its AI products. Chairman and MD Bhanu Chopra said shifting travel demand is increasing customers’ reliance on data and AI. He said RateGain’s priorities included adding customers, increasing their use of its platform, and extending AI into more of their daily operations. In H2 FY27, the company plans to take the combined RateGain and Sojern offering to more customers. RateGain reported a total pipeline of ₹660 Cr and new contract wins worth ₹277.7 Cr. The company’s employee headcount stood at 1,244 at the end of September, up 42.8% YoY. Shares of RateGain ended today’s trading session 3.3% higher at ₹819.50 apiece on the BSE.

title: [Update] Exclusive: RapidClaims In Talks To Raise $30 Mn
title_bn: [Update] Exclusive: RapidClaims In Talks To Raise $30 Mn
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Update | November 5, 19:43 After the story was published, RapidClaims founder and CEO Dushyant Mishra said the startup is…
paragraph1: SUMMARYRapidClaims is in talks to raise around $30 Mn in a funding round led by WestBridge Capital at a valuation of about $200 Mn, sources told Inc42 The proposed fundraise comes amid investor bets on healthcare automation startups, including recent rounds raised by Confido Health and Consint.AI. Existing investors Accel and Together Fund are likely to participate in the round, which is expected to be the startup’s Series B. Update | November 5, 19:43 After the story was published, RapidClaims founder and CEO Dushyant Mishra said the startup is not in talks with WestBridge Capital to raise any funding round. He also said that the $200 Mn valuation figure is “incorrect”. Original | October 5, 18:22 AI-powered SaaS startup RapidClaims is in talks to raise around $30 Mn in a funding round led by WestBridge Capital at a valuation of about $200 Mn, sources told Inc42.
paragraph2: The round is expected to be its Series B, with existing investors Accel and Together Fund likely to participate, the sources added. RapidClaims did not respond to questions sent by Inc42, while WestBridge Capital declined to comment. Founded in 2023 by Dushyant Mishra, Abhinay Vyas, and Jot Sarup Singh, RapidClaims builds AI-powered revenue cycle management (RCM) software that helps healthcare providers automate medical coding, improve clinical documentation, prevent insurance claim denials, and recover outstanding payments. The startup primarily caters to healthcare providers in the US, helping them address billing errors, rejected claims, and delays in reimbursements. Automating Healthcare Revenue Workflows RapidClaims’ products include RapidCode for medical coding, RapidVBC for clinical documentation and risk adjustment, and RapidRecovery for managing denied claims, automating appeals, and detecting underpayments. The platform integrates with healthcare providers’ existing electronic health record systems.
paragraph3: It serves physician groups, hospitals, health systems, federally qualified health centres (FQHCs), and ambulatory surgery centres, among other healthcare organisations. The startup is also developing inpatient coding capabilities with design partners, extending its automation tools to coding for hospital admissions. In April 2025, RapidClaims raised $8 Mn in a Series A round led by Accel, with participation from Together Fund. It also disclosed that it had previously raised $3 Mn in seed funding. RapidClaims had earmarked the Series A proceeds for expanding its go-to-market efforts, strengthening its technology and product capabilities, and growing its sales and marketing teams. At the time, the startup said it had grown sixfold over the preceding four months and served a double-digit client base.
paragraph4: It was also looking to expand its presence among FQHCs, physician groups, outpatient facilities, and ambulatory surgery centres. Investors Bet On Automation The proposed fundraise comes amid increasing investor interest in startups looking to automate healthcare administration and insurance workflows. In October, Confido Health raised $12.5 Mn in a Series A extension led by Z47, taking its total Series A funding to $22.5 Mn. The startup develops AI agents for tasks including appointment scheduling, insurance verification, prescription refills, and payment collection.
paragraph5: Meanwhile, Consint.AI raised ₹22 Cr to expand internationally and develop its AI capabilities for fraud detection and claims processing. Its products automate claims processing, digitise documents, and standardise healthcare records.

title: I downloaded the first third-party app store from Google Play, and I’m hopeful for what’s next
title_bn: I downloaded the first third-party app store from Google Play, and I’m hopeful for what’s next
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Aptoide Games is a decent first start, but it leaves me waiting for more.
paragraph1: Andrew Grush / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: Third-party app stores have been part of the Android experience since literally its earliest days, with the SlideME store predating Google’s official Android Market by several months. Since then we’ve seen plenty of other third-party stores rise up, but they’ve always required extra hoops on the user’s end, like sideloading. That’s no longer the case, as Google Play recently added its very first officially authorized third-party store.This is a major shift in Google’s behavior, but it didn’t come from kindness. Epic Games spent years fighting a legal and PR battle against Apple’s and Google’s app store monopolies. The effort paid off, as it led to several changes, including the passing of anti-monopoly laws like Europe’s Digital Markets Act (DMA). These laws require Google to open up the platform to allow competing storefronts.So far, the effort has been fairly tepid, though it seems many more could be coming later this year. Thankfully, at least one such storefront has made it off the ground: Aptoide Games.
paragraph2: Let’s take a look at how easy it is to install, as well as my general thoughts on the future of third-party app stores.Are you excited about third party app stores coming to Google Play?0 votesInstalling is a piece of cake, and so is using itAndrew Grush / Android AuthorityAs someone who has downloaded countless third-party app stores, I’m used to a little friction here. What I found was basically a one-click installation process that’s no different from installing Angry Birds. While it’s not exactly prominently advertised, finding Aptoide Games was as easy as using the search bar. After that, I tapped “Install,” and in less than a minute, the app store opened and was ready.The first official third-party app store is laid out similarly to Google Play, with a bottom bar of shortcuts to different sections and an easy way to search for specific apps. The layout is clean, easy to use, and feels much more polished than some of the less-refined sideloaded stores I’ve tested over the years.Installing it was easy, though it also felt a bit redundant next to Google Play.
paragraph3: The other thing I learned quickly is that this wasn’t a barren storefront, as it pretty much had every game I could imagine. The catch is that many of these games aren’t actually hosted by Aptoide Games at all, due to a program called the Play Catalog Access Program. This program was part of the legal rulings against Google in the Epic Games lawsuit and basically grants any third-party app store full access to Google’s library. As you can imagine, there are restrictions and rules here, which is partially why Aptoide Games has been the only officially approved candidate so far.Now, to be fair, it’s not just Google-hosted apps. Aptoide Games has a small share of exclusive apps, including those with special reward incentives. In many ways, though, the experience felt a bit redundant next to Google Play. I fear that could be true of other app stores available from Google Play in the future, but it is still too early to tell for sure.I love the potential here, but am also realistic about the limitsAndy Walker / Android AuthorityThere’s a reason that there’s only one official third-party app store so far.
paragraph4: As you might have guessed, publishing a third-party app store requires going through more hoops than publishing an ordinary app. Google’s own documentation has the exact guidelines for those who want to dive deeper, but basically Google requires every app store to ensure a few things: Stores must offer open access with clear, non-discriminatory policies regarding which apps and services they offer. All apps on a store must have clear developer authorization and IP compliance. Certain security, privacy, and safety standards must be met. This includes following Google Play policies, “with the exception of policies that are not applicable to third-party app stores, such as the Payments policy.” All new apps added to a storefront must be signed off by Google, and failure to do so can result in a third-party store being delisted. Those are just a few of the bigger rules. Still, Google says it will occasionally audit random samples of third-party catalogs and that a store must not exceed a 2% content-policy violation rate across audited apps. In addition to quite a few rules, Google also charges a $15,000 upfront annual service fee to perform the necessary security and policy reviews on an app store.
paragraph5: It will also invoice developers if review costs exceed $10,000 per month.If I’m honest, I have a feeling that the Google Play-focused third-party app store experience will likely remain a curated, partial experience. There’s a reason we didn’t get the full-blown Aptoide market here, after all. The good news is this also isn’t Google’s only program from the sounds of it. In addition to Google Play adding select, highly niche stores like Aptoide Games, Google has a broader plan that will bypass some of Android’s recent sideloading restrictions and make it easier to sideload approved app stores as well.Between two similar but slightly different approaches to third-party app stores, it’s clear that third-party app stores will have a larger presence than ever before. It’s also clear Google will do its best to make the process difficult and expensive, which likely rules out some of the smaller, independent open-source stores out there.Still, even with the program somewhat held back by Google, I’m excited to see how it plays out. As sideloading gets harder, adding select curated app stores to Google Play and making it easier to sideload approved stores will only make Android stronger and will help keep it from turning into a walled garden, for better or worse.

This includes following Google Play policies, “with the exception of policies that are not applicable to third-party app stores, such as the Payments policy.” All new apps added to a storefront must be signed off by Google, and failure to do so can result in a third-party store being delisted. Those are just a few of the bigger rules. Still, Google says it will occasionally audit random samples of third-party catalogs and that a store must not exceed a 2% content-policy violation rate across audited apps. In addition to quite a few rules, Google also charges a $15,000 upfront annual service fee to perform the necessary security and policy reviews on an app store.
bangla_paragraph5: It will also invoice developers if review costs exceed $10,000 per month.If I’m honest, I have a feeling that the Google Play-focused third-party app store experience will likely remain a curated, partial experience. There’s a reason we didn’t get the full-blown Aptoide market here, after all. The good news is this also isn’t Google’s only program from the sounds of it. In addition to Google Play adding select, highly niche stores like Aptoide Games, Google has a broader plan that will bypass some of Android’s recent sideloading restrictions and make it easier to sideload approved app stores as well.Between two similar but slightly different approaches to third-party app stores, it’s clear that third-party app stores will have a larger presence than ever before. It’s also clear Google will do its best to make the process difficult and expensive, which likely rules out some of the smaller, independent open-source stores out there.Still, even with the program somewhat held back by Google, I’m excited to see how it plays out. As sideloading gets harder, adding select curated app stores to Google Play and making it easier to sideload approved stores will only make Android stronger and will help keep it from turning into a walled garden, for better or worse.

title: Spacetech Startup Cosmoserve Nets $6 Mn, Eyes Commercialisation By 2028
title_bn: Spacetech Startup Cosmoserve Nets $6 Mn, Eyes Commercialisation By 2028
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 Mn in a seed funding round led by Japan-based Rebright Partners. While Aranya Holdings and…
paragraph1: SUMMARYCosmoserve raised $6 Mn in a seed funding round led by Rebright Partners and inaugurated India’s first private space debris removal facility in Hyderabad It aims to launch another mission in the coming months to validate its soft robotic capture technology to remove defunct satellites and orbital debris from space Following this and another tech demonstration next year, Cosmoserve aims to start commercial operations by 2028 Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 Mn in a seed funding round led by Japan-based Rebright Partners. While Aranya Holdings and Naandi Ventures also participated in the round, existing investors AUM Ventures and Shakti VC doubled down on their erstwhile bet. The startup shared plans to utilise the fresh capital to support tech demonstrations, fuel two upcoming missions, as well enhance the operations of its recently unveiled Hyderabad facility. Cosmoserve has now raised over $9 Mn since inception last year. The startup has doubled its valuation since it raised pre-seed funding in September, founder Chiranjeevi Phanindra told Inc42. The exact valuation is yet to be discerned.
paragraph2: For context, the startup is building tech to remove defunct satellites and orbital debris from space and reduce the collision risks for operational spacecraft in a cost effective manner. It plans on optimising costs by setting up features within its craft that will allow it to refuel in-orbit and remove multiple pieces of debris in a single mission. The startup made its first tech demonstration, Mission Embrace-1, aboard Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket. The mission was designed to test the startup’s soft robotic capture system that removes space debris, but the system’s robotic petals failed to deploy as intended. Cosmoserve claims to have now identified and addressed potential issues with the thermal mechanism used to release the petals and the impact of low temperatures on the system, according to Phanindra. The startup is now gearing up for Embrace-2, an upgraded version of the mission to validate its upgraded robotic capture mechanism, which is expected to launch in the coming months.
paragraph3: It is also planning a full-scale demonstration of its debris-removal capabilities, aiming to break a world record by approaching within 10 m of a dead satellite. Phanindra, who served close to 15 years with the ISRO before setting up Cosmoserve in June 2025, believes that the startup would be able to complete all tech demos by 2027 and start commercial operations by 2028. “We have several letters of intent from satellite constellation operators – one from the US, one from Europe and two from India. They have to abide by the regulation for removing the dead satellite from space … so we are aiming to get one paid customer before actual commercial operations begin,” he added. Cosmoserve’s Base 1 Alongside the funding announcement, Cosmoserve inaugurated its new space debris removal facility in Hyderabad named Base 1 today, in an event attended by union minister of state Dr Jitendra Singh and Telangana IT Minister D Sridhar Babu. Phanindra says that Base 1 is India’s first private and the world’s sixth facility equipped with space vision effects and microgravity simulation.
paragraph4: In simpler terms, Base 1 can recreate conditions that spacecraft and equipment encounter in space, allowing companies to test how their tech will perform before an actual mission. This includes simulating how objects behave in microgravity (near-weightlessness) and how they appear or function under space-like visual conditions. This costs around ₹6 Cr to construct, per Phanindra. Base 1 houses infrastructure for designing, building and testing satellite servicing and space debris recovery missions. This includes an orbital rendezvous and capture lab, an ISO Class 8 clean room for satellite integration, a mission control centre and a microgravity simulation platform. The facility will also support the development of in-orbit satellite repair and refuelling technologies.
paragraph5: Besides, the startup plans to use Base 1 to develop more critical technologies in-house in order to increase its share of local manufacturing from 60% and reduce dependence on imported components such as optics, avionics and space-grade electronics. “Primarily, the core technology we are building is a soft robotic capture system. We have a space robotics innovation lab where the R&D is happening. Then the next technology we are working on is a vision-based navigation system,” the founder told Inc42.
